objectives: The student will be able to analyze a diverse range of laboratory tests and relate the results to history and signalment data, physical examination findings, and post-mortem examination results.
The student will be able to identify additional laboratory testing needs based upon the minimum database or previous testing.
The student will be able to recognize common microscopic findings of clinical significance.
The student will be able to propose differential diagnoses based on initial laboratory test results.
The student will be able to explain pathogeneses and how these relate to laboratory test results in common disorders or diseases.
The student will be able to communicate interpretations for different audiences.
The student will be familiar with types of clinical and anatomic pathology careers, including specific training and job opportunities.
The student will be able to recognize discipline specific knowledge and skills of anatomic and clinical pathologists and their role in diagnostic medicine.
The student will be able to demonstrate proficiency in laboratory procedures, including proper cytology, biopsy, and/or necropsy specimen handling and biosafety.
The student will be able to understand and perform proper cytology, biopsy, and/or necropsy sample collection and preparation procedures, ensuring quality and accuracy.
The student will be able to utilize laboratory equipment and tools effectively for tissue and/or cellular analysis, ensuring safety and precision.
The student will be able to recognize common microscopic and/or gross findings of clinical significance.
The student will be able to develop critical thinking and analytical skills to correlate pathological findings with clinical symptoms and histories.
The student will be able to explain pathogeneses and how these relate to gross and/or microscopic findings or laboratory test results in common disorders or diseases.
The student will be able to communicate diagnostic results effectively through verbal communication and by creating at least one written report.
topics: Anatomic pathology pathway-if selected by student
Clinical pathology pathway-if selected by student

objectives: Students will be able to define common terms and methodologies used in forensic investigations.
Students will be able to describe how to collect and properly preserve samples for evidence during a forensic necropsy.
Students will be able to describe the key features that distinguish cases involving animal cruelty and abuse from illness and death from naturally occurring disease.
Students will be able to write and evaluate a necropsy report.
Students will be able to identify resources for medicolegal death investigation.
Students will know how to prepare to testify in court.
